ordinance_area_text: Densely populated area means an area extending 200 yards from the exterior boundaries of any five or more parcels or tracts, each one of which is adjacent to at least one other, each parcel or tract being one acre or less in area, and which parcels or tracts each contain a structure designed for human use. ... (b) Prohibited. It shall be unlawful ... for any person to: (1) Discharge a firearm or pneumatic gun: a. Within any densely populated area; ... (c) Exceptions. The provisions of this section shall not be applicable to: ... (2) The use of muzzle-loading rifles during the prescribed open seasons for the hunting of game species as permitted in the city; provided, however, that the use of such muzzle-loading rifle shall be only from a stand located at least ten feet in elevation above the ground ...
method: Computed 2026-11 from the City of Suffolk GIS (suffolkgis.suffolk-va.net/hosting, ALL_GIS_Layers MapServer): all 45,546 tax parcels (layer 271), 58,191 building footprints (layer 237, planimetrics from the city's 2021 aerial photography) and 54,047 address points (layer 272), downloaded with outSR=4326, paged. Projected to UTM 18N. A parcel qualifies if (1) it is one acre or less: the assessor area (Assr_Area) where the city records it in acres, otherwise the GIS polygon area (17,488 parcels have only a 'Base Lot' unit) - 32,307 parcels; and (2) it contains a structure: a building footprint of at least 10 m2 whose representative point lies in the parcel, or an address point in the parcel (address points catch homes built after the 2021 footprints). Adjacency = parcel polygons touching or within 0.5 m (a 2 m tolerance changes the area by <0.1%). Connected groups of 5 or more qualifying parcels (1,656 groups, 27,036 parcels) were unioned and buffered 200 yd (182.88 m), then clipped to the city's own boundary layer (City_of_Suffolk_Boundary FeatureServer). Simplified 3 m, parts < 100 m2 dropped, rounded to 1e-5 deg. Single MultiPolygon feature. Scripts: scratchpad ord-areas/suffolk.py, finalize.py.
notes: 119 km2 = 11.0% of the city. The definition was applied literally, with these readings: (a) 'adjacent' = sharing a boundary in the parcel layer, so lots across a street from each other are NOT adjacent (streets are separate right-of-way, not parcels); a broader 'across the street counts' reading would join more clusters and enlarge the area. (b) The five parcels were read as one connected group. Read word for word, 'each one of which is adjacent to at least one other' would also be met by, e.g., a pair plus a triple that do not touch each other; that reading (any qualifying parcel with at least one qualifying neighbour) gives 15.3% of the city instead of 10.7% before simplification. (c) 'Structure designed for human use' = a mapped building footprint or an address point; footprint-only gives 9.6%, footprint-or-address 10.2% (GIS area) / 10.7% (assessor area, used here). Address points on still-vacant lots in new subdivisions may slightly over-include; sheds and garages large enough to be mapped count as structures. (d) Parcels in neighbouring Chesapeake / Isle of Wight / Southampton were not used, and the area was clipped at the city line. Every densely populated area is built-up land, so the area mostly matters at its 200-yd fringe. Separately, everywhere in Suffolk 54-122(b)(1)b-d forbid discharge within 200 yd of another's occupied/business/storage structure without the owner's permission and within 100 yd of any public street or road; those setbacks are NOT in this polygon. The muzzleloading-rifle exception (c)(2) applies inside this area too (stand at least 10 ft high). Parcel lines are tax-map representations, not surveys.
sources: https://www.suffolkva.us/367/Online-Maps (city GIS disclaimer: 2021 aerial photography and planimetrics)
